Fit a MixSIAR model with the prior-data fitted network

Source: R/run_pfn.R
run_pfn.Rd

Replaces MixSIAR's write_JAGS_model() and run_model(): takes the same data objects and model options and returns the marginal posterior of every diet proportion and model parameter, from the network trained for the chosen error structure. There is no MCMC, so no chain length, burn-in or convergence to check.

Usage

run_pfn(
  mix,
  source,
  discr,
  alpha.prior = 1,
  resid_err = TRUE,
  process_err = TRUE,
  seed = 1,
  cont_values = NULL
)

Arguments

mix, source, discr

The outputs of load_mix_data(), load_source_data() and load_discr_data().

alpha.prior

Dirichlet prior on the global diet: one number for every source (MixSIAR's default 1) or one per source, in source$source_names order.

resid_err, process_err

The error structure, as in MixSIAR: both TRUE (Residual * Process, MixSIAR's default), or only one of them.

seed

Seed for the random level assignments the network averages over.

cont_values

For a continuous effect: the values (original units) to report the diet at. By default 25 values over the observed range.

Value

An object of class pfn_fit: summary (one row per diet proportion, with MixSIAR's quantiles and row names such as p.global.Deer), parameters (random-effect SDs, residual error multipliers, covariate slopes), the bar probabilities behind each marginal (for posterior_draws()), and the model options. It holds only R objects, so it can be saved with saveRDS().

Details

The network gives each quantity's marginal posterior, not joint draws: the marginal means of one diet need not sum to exactly 1, and sums, differences or ratios of proportions cannot be computed from the output.

Data, priors and model options outside what the networks were trained for (for example more than 8 sources or 4 tracers) are refused with a message saying which limit was exceeded.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "MixSIARPFN")
mix <- load_mix_data(x("wolves_consumer.csv"), iso_names = c("d13C", "d15N"),
                     factors = c("Region", "Pack"), fac_random = c(TRUE, TRUE),
                     fac_nested = c(FALSE, TRUE), cont_effects = NULL)
source <- load_source_data(x("wolves_sources.csv"), source_factors = "Region",
                           conc_dep = FALSE, data_type = "means", mix)
discr <- load_discr_data(x("wolves_discrimination.csv"), mix)
fit <- run_pfn(mix, source, discr)
fit
} # }
